Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From re- +‎ *staurō, from Proto-Italic *stauros, from Proto-Indo-European *sth₂u-ro-, from *steh₂- (“to stand”). Particularly close cognate with Sanskrit स्थूर (sthūrá, “big, strong”), Proto-Germanic *stōraz (“big, strong”).[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [rɛsˈtau̯.roː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [resˈtaːu̯.ro]

Verb

[edit]

restaurō (present infinitive restaurāre, perfect active restaurāvī, supine restaurātum); first conjugation

  1. to restore, rebuild, reestablish, renew
